ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the x-axis and y-axis at points A and B respectively, and passes through the point $D\left(-2,6\right)$. It intersects the graph of the direct proportionality function $y=3x$ at point C, where the x-coordinate of point C is 1. What is the area of $\triangle BOC$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the x-axis and y-axis at points A and B respectively, and passes through the point $D\left(-2,6\right)$. It intersects the graph of the direct proportionality function $y=3x$ at point C, where the x-coordinate of point C is 1. What is the area of $\triangle BOC$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin; a straight line slanting upward to the right is labeled y=3x and passes through the origin; another straight line slanting downward to the right is labeled y=kx+b, it intersects the y-axis at B, intersects the x-axis at A, and intersects y=3x on the right side at C; point D is located on this straight line slanting downward to the right and is at the upper left. Reasoning: It is known that the abscissa of C is 1, and C is on y=3x, so C=(1,3). Also because the straight line y=kx+b passes through D(-2,6) and C(1,3), its slope is (3-6)/(1-(-2))=-3/3=-1. Therefore the equation of this straight line is y=-x+b. Substitute C(1,3), obtaining 3=-1+b, so b=4, that is, the straight line is y=-x+4. It intersects the y-axis at B, so when x=0, y=4, B=(0,4). In triangle BOC, OB is a line segment on the y-axis, with length 4; the horizontal distance from point C to the y-axis is equal to its abscissa 1. Therefore the area is 1/2×4×1=2.
